clue.text: First and foremost, some beer — usually pints — knocked back here?

definitions.text: First and foremost, some beer — usually pints — knocked back here?

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, and here the chosen letters are turned back to front
the foremost part of each of the next four words is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A drinker's description of the local where beer, mostly by the pint, is downed.
explanation.walkthrough: Initial letters S, B, U, P are read backwards; the whole clue is also the definition, since pints are knocked back in such places.
explanation.definitionFit: Taverns are exactly the places where beer is served by the pint and swallowed.

clue.text: Drop I'm surprised can be squeezed into pint

indicators.note: something squeezed into a container is pushed inside it, so these letters go within the other piece

parts.note: LUMME (lummy) is an old British exclamation of surprise, roughly 'well I never'

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how a whole drop of liquid could fit into a pint glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' looks like a drop of liquid that might fit in a pint, but it is the verb meaning to fall.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall steeply or suddenly is to drop sharply; both verbs describe a rapid descent.

clue.text: Stakes placed all round collieries? That's mad

definitions.note: the clue phrase points to the quality of being mad, a noun, as the answer is

indicators.note: pieces placed all round something enclose it, so one set of letters wraps the other

parts.note: stakes are posts or rods, so bars
collieries are coal pits, i.e. mines

explanation.surface: Someone thinks fencing stakes all round the coal pits would be crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Barmy is British slang for crazy, so the noun means craziness, the state that is mad.

clue.text: Garment sends girth out of all proportion

indicators.note: a shape out of all proportion is distorted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An item of clothing makes the wearer's waistline look enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose gown worn to bed is a kind of clothing, so garment is its general category.

clue.text: Piece of music in final part of concert having men standing up

indicators.note: the final part of a word is its closing letter
in a down answer, something standing up is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: OR (other ranks) is the military abbreviation for ordinary soldiers, i.e. men

explanation.surface: A concert ends with a piece during which the men rise to their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening passage played before the main part of a song is itself a short musical piece.

clue.text: Flat racing after horse badly hurt? That's not entirely correct

indicators.note: the shuffled first word comes after the abbreviation for horse

parts.note: H is a slang abbreviation for heroin, known as horse

indicators.note: letters racing about are moving wildly, so they are rearranged
something done badly is botched, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A racing tip: a horse badly hurt can't run on the Flat, which isn't quite accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: Flat racing is British horse racing without jumps; 'Flat racing' tempts as a phrase but 'racing' shuffles FLAT to ALFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement only partly true is one that is not wholly accurate.

clue.text: Stopping and starting music, dancing out in sun

parts.note: disco is a style of dance music

indicators.note: letters dancing move about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Disco music plays fitfully as people dance outside in the sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that keeps halting and resuming is intermittent, broken rather than continuous.

clue.text: Directions to get round Roman road in French spa town

indicators.note: one piece gets round the other by enclosing it

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
VIA is the Latin word for road, as in Via Appia

explanation.surface: Instructions for finding a way round an old Roman road to a French resort.
explanation.definitionFit: The spa town on Lake Geneva is famous for its bottled mineral water.

clue.text: Indications about what new job seeker does

parts.note: indications are signs
on means about or concerning, as in a talk on birds

explanation.surface: A careers adviser describes signs of what an unemployed person does next.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an unemployed person registers for benefit, a phrase used colloquially for joining the dole.
explanation.definitionFit: Registering as jobless at the benefits office is the first step a new seeker of work takes.

clue.text: Virtuous prude drinks type of milk? The opposite

indicators.note: one who drinks takes something inside, so one piece contains the other
this reverses the roles stated, so the milk holds the prude rather than the prude holding the milk

parts.note: UHT is ultra-heat-treated long-life milk
a prig is a priggish, prudish person

explanation.surface: A prim person sips some kind of milk, or perhaps it's the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A morally honest, principled person is good and righteous, so virtuous.

clue.text: Won art auction, it's understood

definitions.meaning: taken literally, someone who won at an art sale acquired a painting
the idiom means one grasped what was meant

explanation.surface: Someone successfully bids for a painting, and the meaning is clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasping the situation is captured by the idiom of seeing the whole image, i.e. comprehending.

clue.text: Writer the French celebrate

parts.note: LES is French for 'the' (plural)
to sing is to celebrate in song, as in singing someone's praises

explanation.surface: An author celebrated by the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris Lessing, the Nobel prizewinning novelist, is the author meant; Gotthold Lessing was a German dramatist.

clue.text: It's wet: motorist should avoid high terrain

indicators.note: the letters to be avoided are left out of the word

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor in England

explanation.surface: Driving advice: when it's raining, motorists should keep off the high ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Damp and moist both describe something slightly soaked with water.

clue.text: Excitedly go to uni, getting tips for graduates' expenses

indicators.note: done excitedly suggests agitation, so these letters are rearranged
the tips of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Students head off eagerly to university, with advice on graduates' spending.
explanation.definitionFit: Money that goes out, spending and costs, is the plural noun for expenditure.

clue.text: Queen's insistence that Royal Variety Performance will happen?

definitions.text: Queen's insistence that Royal Variety Performance will happen?

parts.words: Queen's insistence that Royal Variety Performance will happen?
parts.note: the monarch insisting her annual variety gala goes ahead would use the showbusiness motto; it is also a song by the rock band Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch demands that her annual charity variety show proceed regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Variety Performance is a British televised charity show attended by royalty; Queen also recorded a song with this title.
explanation.definitionFit: The theatrical saying that a performance must proceed whatever happens fits a royal insisting her show goes ahead.

clue.text: Loud, belligerent type, I'll guarantee

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a noisy speechifier about fighting: someone who rants about combat
the person who vouches for or underwrites something, a guarantor

explanation.surface: A noisy, aggressive person boasts of their own reliability.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantor gives a formal assurance, so the person promising to guarantee is described.

clue.text: Start to spout after swallowing one drink

indicators.note: something swallowing takes another thing inside it

parts.note: to spout is to speechify, i.e. orate
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a spirit drink

explanation.surface: Someone begins holding forth after downing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To arise or begin is to spring from a source, the verb's core sense.

clue.text: Husband avoids misadventure with that woman over in guest house getting the wrong idea

indicators.note: the letter for husband is avoided, so it is dropped from the word

parts.note: a misadventure is a mishap
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: a pension is a continental boarding house

indicators.note: turned over means reversed

parts.note: her refers to a woman already mentioned

explanation.surface: A husband dodges trouble with a woman at a guest house, but has misunderstood the situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns HER to REH, which goes into PENSION; 'avoids' removes H from MISHAP to give MISAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A misunderstanding is a mistaken belief, a false notion about something.

clue.text: Lost flipping phone card

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the letters are read backwards; also a mild British expletive

parts.note: to dial is to phone someone
a SIM card goes in a mobile phone

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry: the wretched phone card has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' turns DIALSIM to read backwards; it looks like the British mild curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put in the wrong place and missing has been mislaid, so lost.

clue.text: Very small lion man shot

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or broken, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tiny hunter shoots a lion.
explanation.definitionFit: A token or minimal amount, such as a nominal fee, is tiny.

clue.text: School with mean person teaching one who's not very bright?

parts.note: low means mean or base, as in a low trick
a coach is a tutor or trainer

explanation.surface: A school where a tight-fisted teacher instructs a dim pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a stretch: a slow person is 'slow' in the sense of being not very quick-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: A sluggish or dull-witted person is dismissively called slow, so not bright.

clue.text: Group's vocal slips, every now and then

indicators.note: taking letters every now and then means every second one

explanation.surface: A band's singer makes occasional mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manchester rock band led by the Gallagher brothers is a famous pop group.

clue.text: Virgin removing top in hurry

indicators.note: in a down answer the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a virgin is chaste

explanation.surface: A Virgin train passenger in a rush takes off a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed and urgency, haste and hurry are synonyms as nouns.

clue.text: I … er … join operation to locate drug

parts.note: um is a hesitation sound like er

explanation.surface: A hesitant recruit agrees to join an operation to find narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: The narcotic made from poppy sap is a classic drug.

clue.text: Storm a sailor mentioned

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so the letters come from the way the words sound

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman is named in connection with a storm at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a position is to attack it, so storm as a verb or noun means an attack.

clue.text: Hold up in South American train: robbers' leader escapes

parts.note: US stands for United States, so American

indicators.note: the letter that escapes leaves the word
a word's leader is its first letter

explanation.surface: A hold-up on a South American train where the gang's chief gets away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold up' looks like a robbery, but it means support.
explanation.definitionFit: To support or bear weight from below is to keep something up.

clue.text: Put off food consumed around middle of afternoon

parts.note: a dish is a prepared food

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other

parts.note: eaten means consumed

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A meal eaten mid-afternoon leaves someone with no appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage someone is to put them off, sapping their spirit.

clue.text: Private room vice-chancellor's reserved

indicators.note: something reserved is kept or held within, so the letters are concealed in the words

explanation.surface: A university head has a room kept for their own use.
explanation.definitionFit: A small room for one person, as for a monk or prisoner, is a private chamber.
